title: Small-leaved Lime: Ancient Limes You Can Visit
meta_description: For centuries the local court sat outdoors under a lime, where everyone could hear it. Twelve old limes mapped, from Ljubljana to Warsaw.
intro: For centuries in this part of Europe you were tried under one of these. The Gerichtslinde, the court lime, was a real institution: a broad tree on the village square with benches beneath it, where the local court sat in the open because everybody could then see and hear what had been decided. Small-leaved lime was usually the species chosen, since it lives long, takes heavy pruning and builds exactly that kind of wide low crown. The habit of gathering under them outlasted the courts. Carters running between Vienna and Trieste stopped under Ljubljana's Furmanska lipa to buy hay for their horses, and that tree, planted in 1626, turns 400 in 2026. Zurich has been replanting the same hilltop ever since a chronicle recorded 52 limes going in at once in 1474, and twelve limes across ten cities are mapped here.
